$schema_note: Migrations that stay in this directory as history but whose effect is deliberately ABSENT from every database — withdrawn at the owner's direction, or superseded by a later file whose work they would undo. A file listed here is not a backlog. `migration-drift` reports it under WITHDRAWN rather than NOT APPLIED, and FAILS if any object named in `absent` exists, because then this declaration is false. Mission Control reads this file from the prime and neither sends a listed file to any clone nor counts it as a hole, so it cannot hold back the files after it. `apply-migration.yml` refuses to apply a listed file. `scripts/security/check-migration-withdrawals.mjs` checks every entry: the file exists, every `absent` object is one the file itself creates, and a named successor exists. The files are NOT deleted: an applied migration's bytes are what `applied-body-digests.txt` protects, and a deleted file is a gap in the record of what ran. To reverse a withdrawal, remove its entry in the same pull request that records the decision, then apply the file.
